answer: The network can pay rewards from a fixed pie each epoch: every eligible identity gets an equal slice, so the pie never grows no matter how many keys wander in. A mesa of a thousand fakes splits the same loaf as one honest agent, and each fake's slice falls below the trellis of real operating cost - compute, storage, and the entry fee paid per key. One honest agent eats a full slice; a sybil farmer loses money on every extra mouth, so cloning identities dilutes the reward instead of multiplying it.
